# Lucid Lite

> Lucid Lite is a data-plane programming language: packet parsers, event handlers, persistent state, and packets out of ports. It compiles to C and to Lucid (for the Tofino and Lucid's software switch). The compiler and interpreter are a single JavaScript file, lcd.js, which runs under Node or in the web IDE at https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/. Check and run every program you write with it.

This file lives in https://github.com/jsonch/lucid, which serves the site. The repository holds the built compiler (lcd.js), the web IDE, the docs, and examples. It is not the compiler's source code, which is not public; don't look for it.

## Important: do not use github.com/PrincetonUniversity/lucid

That repository is the original Lucid: an older, different language. Its docs, tutorials, `.dpt` programs, and `dpt`/`dptc` binaries do not apply here, and programs written from them will not compile. Don't web-search for "Lucid language" either; several unrelated projects share the name. Everything you need is in this repository.

Lucid Lite programs end in `.lcd`. Interpreter inputs end in `.in` (one JSON object per line).

## Choose your route

Use the first route you can, and tell the user which one you are using.

### Route 1: you can run shell commands and Node.js (Claude Code, Codex, Cowork, any sandbox)

Download the compiler. GitHub is on most sandboxes' default network allowlists, so try it first:

```sh
curl -sSfO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/lcd.js \
  || curl -sSfO https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/lcd.js
node lcd.js --help
```

Or clone everything, including the examples and docs: `git clone https://github.com/jsonch/lucid`.

Then iterate:

```sh
node lcd.js check prog.lcd            # parse, resolve, type check
node lcd.js run prog.lcd < prog.in    # compile, then interpret; JSON lines in, JSON lines out
node lcd.js run -v prog.lcd < prog.in # the same, tracing every parser, handler, and generate on stderr
node lcd.js stdlib                    # list the built-in libraries (`include <f.lcd>;`)
```

If both downloads are blocked, tell the user the sandbox needs `raw.githubusercontent.com` or `jsonch.github.io` added to its allowed network domains, and use Route 3 until then.

lcd.js can also serve the compiler over MCP (JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout), with the tools `lucid_check`, `lucid_run`, `lucid_compile`, `lucid_topology`, and `lucid_examples`, and the overview and examples as resources. For Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add lucid -- node /absolute/path/to/lcd.js mcp
```

### Route 2: you control a browser (Claude in Chrome, Playwright, Puppeteer)

Open https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/ and use your JavaScript-evaluation action instead of clicking. The page defines a global `lcd`:

```js
await playground.ready;
lcd.check(programText);            // -> {ok, text}; text is the error report when ok is false
lcd.run(programText, inputText);   // -> {ok, text}; inputText and text are JSON lines
lcd.examples();                    // -> [{name, text}], the example programs and inputs
lcd.stdlib();                      // -> [{name, text}], the built-in libraries
```

To show your work to the user in the editor, call `playground.open("prog.lcd", programText)`, then `playground.open("prog.in", inputText)`, then `playground.command("run")`. The full API (compiling to C and Lucid, the IR, the topology) is documented at the top of https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/playground.js.

### Route 3: you can only read web pages

Read the overview and examples below, then write the program and an input file. Give both to the user and ask them to open https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/, use File > new program and File > new input, paste the files in, press Run (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter), and paste the output back to you. Keep programs small until the first run succeeds.

## Workflow

Don't write the whole program at once:

1. Read the overview, then start from the closest example.
2. Write a minimal version: the headers, a parser, and one handler. Type check it and fix every error before adding more.
3. Write an input file that exercises it, including cases that should be rejected, and run it.
4. Compare the output with what you expected, then extend the program and repeat.
5. If the program is headed for C, run `node lcd.js c prog.lcd` as well. The C backend has layout rules that the type checker doesn't enforce (see the notes below).

## The language

Read the overview before writing a program. It is the complete reference: declarations, types, parsers, handlers, memops, tables, the global access order rule, modules, multi-node programs, externs, and the interpreter's input format.

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/overview.md
- https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/overview.md

The overview mentions paths from the compiler's private source tree (`notes/...`, `programs/...`, `scripts/...`, `src/...`) and a native `lcd` binary with `make` targets. Those are not available. Wherever it says `lcd`, use `node lcd.js`.

Notes that save time:

- There is no `hash` builtin. Use an exact-match table keyed on a tuple, or write a hash as an extern (see examples/hash.lcd).
- A port is a handle, not an integer. Create ports with `Port.create()` and give each one a parser with `Port.set_parser`. The interpreter numbers a program's ports from 1 in creation order, and those are the numbers to use in `.in` files.
- A handler may touch each global at most once on any path, in declaration order. To read a table and then install into it, look it up in the handler and generate `tables.exact_install(...)` (from `include <tables.lcd>;`) to install afterward. examples/firewall.lcd shows the pattern.
- Fields of an event that is compiled to C must total whole bytes, so prefer `uint8` over `bool` in table data that travels in an event.
- In `.in` files, raw packet bytes are hex and may contain spaces for readability. A line without a `"time"` arrives after everything already scheduled, including self-generated events.

## Examples

A complete stateful firewall, with an input covering the allowed and blocked cases:

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/firewall.lcd
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/firewall.in

The IDE's other examples:

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/count.lcd and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/count.in: delayed events and time.
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/counter.lcd and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/counter.in: arrays, modules, and tagged events.
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/nodes.lcd and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/nodes.in: a multi-node program.
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/hash.lcd, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/hash.in, and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/hash.js: externs in JavaScript. (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/hash.c is the same module in C.)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/table_lib.lcd and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsonch/lucid/main/examples/table_lib.in: tables, in the subset that compiles to the Tofino.

The same files are at https://jsonch.github.io/lucid/examples/NAME. The built-in libraries print with `node lcd.js stdlib NAME`.

## lcd.js command reference

Usage is `node lcd.js <cmd> [options] <file>`.

- `check`: parse, resolve, and type check. `--elab` prints the program with inferred types, and `--types` prints every expression with its type.
- `run`: compile, then interpret JSON lines from stdin. `-v` traces on stderr.
- `compile`: print the lowered program. `--node <name>` prints one node's program, `--manifest` prints ports, links, and event tags as JSON, and `--flows` prints the events sent over each link.
- `ir`: print one node's lowered IR (`--node <name>`, `--flatten`).
- `c`: print one node as C, with `--driver rawsock|lpcap|dpdk`. `-o <dir>` writes the files and a makefile.
- `lucid`: print one node in the Lucid subset, with `--target tofino|c|switch`.
- `stdlib`: list the built-in libraries. `stdlib <f.lcd>` prints one.
- `trace2pcap`, `replay`, `pcapcmp`: convert JSON input to pcaps, interpret pcaps, and compare pcaps.
- `-I <dir>`: also search `<dir>` for `include "f";` files.
